mechanism: Both drugs are nephrotoxic and can cause acute kidney injury through different mechanisms—chlorthalidone via volume depletion and electrolyte abnormalities, and tenofovir via direct tubular toxicity—resulting in additive renal impairment and potential tenofovir accumulation.
action: Monitor renal function (eGFR, serum creatinine, urinalysis) at baseline and regularly during concurrent use; consider alternative antihypertensive agents in patients with baseline renal impairment or risk factors; ensure adequate hydration and evaluate for proteinuria or proximal tubule dysfunction.
